data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A decentralized network of small services is more resilient to correlated failure than a redundant monolith because its primary defense is operational heterogeneity, which prevents the propagation of single-point-of-failure (SPOF) triggers that bypass internal redundancy.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The decentralized services share a common critical upstream dependency (e.g., a single cloud provider's regional API).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The services converge on a standardized 'industry-best' stack that reinstates homogeneity.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The 'fragmentation firewall' effect: while a monolith achieves redundancy through replication (increasing the surface area for a single bug to crash all nodes), a decentralized network achieves resilience through divergence in software stacks, kernels, and operational cadences, ensuring that a specific trigger (e.g., a leap second bug or a specific library vulnerability) only affects a subset of the network.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
